title: Closed restriction preserves the supported finite-field coefficient-topology defect
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. Put $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using all continuous maps on every profinite set $P$, and $A_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for each finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, with its restricted norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $R_V=p_V^*R$ for these condensed rings on each scheme $V$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work with internal module objects on small pro-étale sites and their ordinary uncompleted derived categories in the fixed indexing universe [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention].
Also put
$$C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega):f(P)\subseteq F\text{ for some finite intermediate }F/\mathbf Q_\ell\},$$
the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $c:C\hookrightarrow B$ be the inclusion of functions. Fix a closed immersion $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of qcqs schemes, with no quasi-compactness assumption on its open complement [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose that for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, without a common annihilator, the actual restrictions
$$H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\longrightarrow H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$$
are bijective for all $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Choose a finite chain $W=V_s\to\cdots\to V_0=T$, each arrow a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix a finite intermediate field $E$ and a pro-étale locally finite free $A_{E,W}$-module $N$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $J_E$ be the composite of module $a_!$ at open arrows and module $a_*$ at closed arrows, with the identity for $s=0$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. For $R=C,B$ define the $A_{E,T}$-module
$$H_R=J_E\operatorname{Res}_{A_{E,W}\to R_W}(R_W\otimes_{A_{E,W}}N),$$
where tensor and exact scalar restriction are the ordinary internal operations [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The inclusion $c_W$ induces the actual map $m:H_C\to H_B$, locally given before $J_E$ by $z\otimes v\mapsto c_W(z)\otimes v$. Let $D_{J,E,N}$ be the cochain complex with $H_C$ in degree $-1$, $H_B$ in degree $0$, differential $m$, and zero elsewhere [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. In the ordinary derived category this is the mapping-cone complex of $H_C[0]\to H_B[0]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then the actual module-derived restriction
$$R\Gamma(T,D_{J,E,N})\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T_0,t^*D_{J,E,N})$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. It is induced by the pullback-adjunction section unit and K-injective resolutions [def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]; $t^*$ uses the coefficient identification pulled back from the point. No finite-coefficient comparison property $\mathsf B_E(t)$ is assumed. Neither endpoint is asserted to vanish, and neither $C\to B$ nor its pullback is asserted to be an isomorphism or flat. This includes arbitrary such finite support chains, the identity chain, empty schemes and $N=0$. No field, characteristic or Noetherian hypothesis on the schemes, no completeness of $\Omega$, and no replacement of its all-continuous functions is imposed.
